newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-ELS SIX HOLES UP ON BROOKS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-ELS SIX HOLES UP ON BROOKS.

text.p: Holder Ernie Els capitalised on a poor display from U.S. PGA champion Mark Brooks to open a six-hole gap in their World Matchplay semifinal on Saturday.

Els, six down himself in Friday's second round clash with Steve Stricker before he won on the last hole, played only mediocre golf against Brooks but it was good enough to put him in command against the faltering 35-year-old Texan.

Assuming Els avoids the sort of collapse which helped him overcome Stricker on Friday, the world number four will be within one match of becoming the first player to win this prestigious title three times in succession in its 33-year history.
"I guess I'm fortunate because Mark did not play anywhere near as good as he can," Els said. "He'll play better this afternoon and I will have to as well. I am not hitting the ball as I want to."
Brooks, struggling with the length of the soggy, 6,957-yard West Course at Wentworth, bogeyed four holes on the front nine including three in succession from the seventh.

He made his only birdie at the long 17th to halve the hole, though his final putt from three feet was conceded. Then he summed up his morning by missing from four feet at the last to lose the hole and leave himself in dire trouble.
Brooks, who went straight to the practice range, said: "I played awful. I have not been swinging well in a few weeks and it has been one experiment after another.
"Today's experiment didn't work too well. However, I am going to try like hell because Ernie is not playing that well."
In the other semifinal, second seed Tom Lehman, the British Open champion, was all square with Vijay Singh of Fiji halfway through their 36-hole match.
Els and Brooks halved the first three holes before the South African, joint second in this year's British Open, won the fourth with a par when Brooks missed the green.
Brooks could not find the green with his second shot at the seventh, eighth and ninth holes either as he fell three behind, Els bogeying the ninth as well.
The American tangled with the trees at the 13th and needed two shots to escape, only to find a bunker. Then Els rammed in a 45-foot putt at the 15th to go five ahead before Brooks's miss at the last.
Singh led Lehman after winning the third hole with a four iron to three feet for a birdie but the American won the sixth and seventh with birdies, the second coming from 18 feet.
Singh levelled at the ninth with a 20-footer but Lehman fired fine iron shots close at the next two holes to go two in front.
Then he bogeyed the 15th and the 16th, where he three-putted from 20 feet, and they halved the last two, Singh making an eight-footer to stay level at the 18th.
"Tom gave me two holes on the run. I hit some bad drives and bad approaches but I got away with it," Singh said.
Lehman said he miscalculated with a nine iron at the 15th, which he termed "a rookie mistake", and added that he was distracted by swirling leaves putting the 16th.
